claims.text: Conventional fabrication of W–Cu composites typically produces voids, phase separation, and imperfect W–Cu interfacial contact.
A machine-learning-optimized SPS thermal-pressure profile will reduce void formation relative to conventional SPS.
A machine-learning-optimized SPS profile will improve W–Cu interfacial bonding relative to conventional SPS.
The proposed reduction in voids and improvement in interfacial bonding will enhance thermal transport.
The proposed process will preserve mechanical durability under fusion-reactor irradiation conditions.
SPS uses heat and pressure to form bonding between powder particles.
SPS provides rapid heating and efficient densification.
Optimizing the SPS thermal-pressure cycle will accelerate densification beyond that obtained with conventional SPS.
The optimized SPS cycle will minimize gas entrapment during W–Cu sintering.
Avoiding excessive processing temperatures will reduce vaporization of low-melting constituents.
Avoiding excessive processing temperatures will prevent phase separation in W–Cu.
A more uniform W–Cu microstructure with fewer interfacial defects will have improved thermal conductivity.
A more uniform W–Cu microstructure with better interfacial bonding will maintain or improve mechanical strength under irradiation.
Current SPS or mechanical-alloying processes often leave residual voids and imperfections.
Residual voids and imperfections from current SPS or mechanical-alloying processes impair thermal transport and may compromise durability.
The intervention is restricted to SPS temperatures below the boiling point of Cu and below the melting point of W.
The effectiveness of the machine-learning optimization depends on the quality and representativeness of its training data.
The optimized SPS profile may not remain effective under processing conditions far outside the machine-learning model's training domain.
